findings.cwe: CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory
findings.finding: Resume and rollback trust operation.path, staged, and backup values deserialized from .agent/runtime/upgrade/transaction.json: read_journal validates only schema_version, inspect joins operation.path directly, apply/restore do not call validate_relative_path, and the removal branches call fs::remove_file directly. A crafted persisted journal can therefore bypass the new specs prohibition, copy bytes from an absolute/traversing staged or backup path into the repository, or delete any accessible absolute/../ path whose supplied preimage matches; apply_workspace_upgrade resumes such a journal before its normal clean-worktree and bundle validation path.
findings.fix: Validate every deserialized operation path with validate_relative_path before inspect/apply/restore, constrain staged and backup to the transaction's generated relative names under its root, and add resume/rollback regressions for specs/, absolute paths, dot traversal, and staged/backup traversal.

findings.cwe: CWE-178: Improper Handling of Case Sensitivity
findings.finding: The specs boundary compares raw UTF-8 text case-sensitively. `Specs/evil` is correctly a distinct allowed path on a case-sensitive filesystem, but on a default case-insensitive macOS filesystem it aliases `specs/evil` and lets a custom package manifest bypass the intended specs/** prohibition; the repository-seed containment guard does not enforce this policy.
findings.fix: Reject a first component equal to specs under at least ASCII case folding for portable manifests, and add mixed-case manifest and CLI regressions on supported platforms.

findings.finding: Apart from filesystem case aliasing and the journal revalidation gap, validate_relative_path safely rejects empty, absolute, backslash-separated, CurDir/ParentDir, .agent/runtime, exact specs, specs/, and trailing-slash variants. ASCII `specs` has no Unicode normalization variant, Unicode lookalikes remain different names, and `specsx/evil` is correctly accepted because it is neither specs nor under specs/.
findings.fix: Confirmation of safe behavior; retain component validation and the exact-or-directory-prefix distinction.

findings.finding: Fresh init calls validate_fresh_target before any scaffold or package write, its target set includes specs, and the only direct specs seed call is the fixed empty specs/adr/.gitkeep at lines 111-115. Bundle files pass PackageBundle::load/load_files validation first. Scaffold sources contain no specs target, while legacy history is parsed through BundleManifest::read and workspace ownership through WorkspaceManifest::validate, both of which share validate_relative_path.
findings.fix: Confirmation of safe behavior for ordinary scaffold, fresh-init, package-manifest, and historical-adoption flows; the persisted transaction journal exception is covered by the first finding.

findings.finding: The ADR and mirrored README/design/requirements claims that managed upgrade does not mutate specs/** and verifies every operation are broader than the current resume/rollback implementation because a persisted journal is not path-validated; the scoped version metadata is internally aligned at 1.0.5 and the reviewed changes contain no credential or secret value.
findings.fix: Fix journal validation and case-insensitive alias handling before retaining the categorical confinement claims, or explicitly qualify the claims until enforcement matches them.

disposition.summary: Two confirmed HIGH path-boundary issues remain: a case-insensitive filesystem alias bypass in managed manifest validation and unvalidated persisted transaction journal paths that can bypass specs confinement and reach arbitrary reads/copies or file deletion. Fresh-init gating, direct seed call inventory, ordinary bundle/workspace manifest validation, version alignment, and secret review were otherwise safe.
